title: enhance: canary + shadow + A/B autorollback workflow and observability improvements
author: Avery Lin
description:
Context: We continue to expand the Unified Rollouts capabilities to make automated rollback decisions safer and more observable across mixed deployment modes (canary, A/B, shadow). This PR adds a set of workflow improvements, tighter metric quorum logic, and new telemetry to reduce false positives and make incident triage faster.

Goals: 1) Improve stability of auto-rollback decisions for canary + shadow + A/B rollouts under noisy metric signals. 2) Add observability hooks and dashboards for rollback decisions and quarantine events. 3) Add safety guards (quarantine stage, metric quorum, cooldown windows) and extend e2e coverage.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a quorum-based metric aggregator that requires a configurable fraction of metrics to exceed thresholds before triggering rollback.
- Adds a quarantine stage to the probe workflow: when an anomaly is detected, traffic is routed to a quarantine probing stage and a short isolation window is used before a full rollback.
- Adds cooldown and progressive rollback windows to prevent flip-flopping of decisions.
- Improves shadow traffic handling: decouple shadow probes from production quota and add sampling controls to reduce noise from large-traffic customers.
- Adds structured decision logging for every autorollback candidate (decision_id, metrics snapshot, contributing metrics list, weights, quorum vote breakdown) to the observability pipeline.
- Exposes new metrics and alerting signals for dashboards: rollout.decision.latency, rollout.quarantine.count, rollout.vote.quorum_fraction, rollout.rollback.rationale_count.
- Adds unit + integration tests for metric quorum logic and quarantine workflow; adds new e2e stability test exercising canary+shadow+A/B flows under synthetic noise.

Checklist: 
- [x] Quorum-based aggregator implementation and tests
- [x] Quarantine stage implementation and routing integration tests
- [x] Structured decision logging and telemetry pipeline integration
- [x] CI e2e tests added for noisy-signal scenarios
- [x] Docs: rollout workflow and configuration reference updated
- [x] Observability: dashboards + alert rules added (Grafana + alertmanager templates)

Commit summary: see `commits` field for a high-level list.

Motivation / Rationale: We observed multiple incidents where single noisy metrics caused premature rollbacks during canary rollouts. The existing rule engine made decisions from simple threshold crossings which amplified noisy telemetry. The quorum approach reduces sensitivity to single-metric jitter, while the quarantine stage buys human/operator time and reduces blast radius for false positives. Structured decision logs enable post-mortem analysis and ML-based future tuning.

Compatibility notes: Default behavior is backwards-compatible: new quorum and quarantine settings are opt-in via rollout policy flags; existing deployments keep previous behavior unless the new flags are enabled.

Related Linear items: ENG-1423, ENG-1768, ENG-1849.

Documentation: Updated docs/redwood-docs/deployments/unified-rollouts.md and rollout-config reference in the repo.

merge_commit_message:
enhance: canary + shadow + A/B autorollback workflow and observability improvements (#118112)

Quorum aggregator, quarantine stage, structured decision logging, metrics and dashboards, e2e tests, docs.
release_notes: Enhanced autorollback workflow for Unified Rollouts: quorum-based metric aggregation, quarantine stage to reduce false positives, improved shadow traffic handling, structured decision logs, new rollout metrics and dashboards, plus e2e tests for noisy signals. Backwards-compatible and opt-in via rollout policy flags.
notes_for_ops: Operators can enable the new workflow via rolloutPolicy.quorum.enabled and configure quorumFraction, quarantineWindowSec, and cooldownWindowSec. Dashboards and alerts deployed to observability namespace: redwood-rollouts (Grafana) and rollout-alerts (Alertmanager).
testing: Added unit tests for quorum and quarantine controller, integration tests for routing and decision logging, and an e2e job that simulates noisy metrics to ensure autorollback stability. CI pipeline includes a daily e2e noise stability run.
performance_impact: Minimal at control-plane level; quorum aggregation adds a small CPU cost during decision evaluation (benchmarked <2ms per decision on typical traffic). No added latency to inference path; quarantine routing uses existing routing primitives.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1902: roll out default policy opt-in across staging clusters
ENG-1910: add historical decision analytics dashboard
ENG-1923: explore ML-assisted threshold tuning from decision logs
